## `ComposedDistributions.jl`

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- Write the epidemiology as distributions
- The probabilistic programming language becomes optional
- A verb grammar for composition over any `Distributions.jl`
  distribution: chains, branches, and `one_of` outcomes
- A composed object scores an observed record *and* simulates a new one
- Parameter uncertainty is an ordinary leaf, not a PPL-specific layer
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
```julia
cfr = 0.12

admission = @uncertain compose((
    path = sequential(
        :onset_admit => LogNormal(Normal(0.0, 0.2), 0.4),
        :admit_outcome => resolve(
            :death => (Gamma(1.5, 1.0), cfr),
            :discharge => Gamma(2.0, 1.5))),
    onset_report = truncated(Gamma(1.5, 1.0); upper = 21.0),
    onset_referral = censored(Gamma(1.0, 2.0); upper = 14.0)))
```

::: {.attribution}
A hospital pathway from the `ComposedDistributions.jl` README, `main`
checked 2026-08-13 · `resolve` picks an outcome with the given
probability, `sequential` and `one_of` are the other two of the three
composition verbs
:::
:::
::::

## Where we are

- `ComposedDistributions.jl` — the verb grammar above
- `CensoredDistributions.jl` — censoring and truncation
- `ConvolvedDistributions.jl` — convolution and quadrature
- `ModifiedDistributions.jl` — transformations that stay distributions
- `ReparameterisedDistributions.jl` — reparameterised sampling
- `DistributionsInference.jl` — the fitting layer, no model macro

::: {.attribution}
All are active EpiAware packages, pushed within the last two days ·
[ComposedDistributions.jl][composed] ·
[CensoredDistributions.jl][censored] · [ConvolvedDistributions.jl][convolved] ·
[ModifiedDistributions.jl][modified] ·
[ReparameterisedDistributions.jl][reparm] ·
[DistributionsInference.jl][dinf]
:::

## `Distributions.jl`

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- A small team maintains the interface everything above leans on
- There is no concrete written definition of the `Distributions.jl`
  interface
- Should we aim to be more generic: anything with a limited set of
  methods, e.g. `rand` and `logpdf`?

::: {.callout-important}
If `Distributions.jl` is a convention rather than a package, the
composed-distributions direction and everything built on it depends on
an interface nobody has pinned down.
:::
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
- The fitting layer is what a probabilistic programming language was
  doing. `DistributionsInference.jl` does it without a model macro
- `CensoredDistributions.jl` does not depend on `Turing.jl`. Nothing in
  `src/` mentions it

::: {.attribution}
[github.com/JuliaStats/Distributions.jl][distjl] ·
`DistributionsInference.jl` README, `main` at `ac84bdf`, read 2026-08-12
:::
:::
::::

## Is Julia the place for this work?

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="68%"}
- JAX has one automatic differentiation system, and everything is
  written against it
- We test seven automatic differentiation configurations in CI and
  cannot tell a user which one is safe for a composed model
- 🤖 I wrote much of this deck and the code behind it with coding
  agents, and I am not sure that is the story to sell to an
  epidemiological audience

::: {.callout-important}
I have argued myself into both answers.
:::
